A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same subobject-level image-tokenization work. Their complete text, figures, mathematical content and references are readable and support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 5 report original CLEVR captioning experiments, including training curves and object-attribute/count accuracies.

after.justification: Section 3.4 and Figure 4 retain those original captioning results. Figure 2 additionally presents segmentation outputs produced by DirectSAM.

M1.justification: V1 describes SAM mask generation followed by mask expansion and gap filling. V2 introduces DirectSAM: a SegFormer-based boundary predictor trained on contour targets, with global/local multiscale prediction merging. SeqAE and the LVLM architecture remain unchanged; the reported LVLM experiments still use MobileSAM-v2.

E1.justification: SA-1B and CLEVR remain the datasets used. V2 additionally uses SA-1B for supervised full-image boundary prediction, beyond the retained segment-autoencoding task, and its qualitative segmentation examples include cartoons alongside photographic scenes. CLEVR captioning coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The quantitative captioning comparison retains the same autoencoding-trained 32-by-32 patch-tokenizer baseline. However, v1 Figure 2 compares unprocessed SAM output with postprocessed segmentation; v2 replaces that qualitative comparison with DirectSAM-only outputs, removing the unprocessed reference.

E3.justification: V2 adds a DirectSAM training protocol: one epoch at 1024-by-1024 resolution followed by 0.6 epoch at 1800-by-1800, with contour preprocessing, Gaussian blur and stage-specific training settings. Its visualizations use multiscale inference. The existing SeqAE and CLEVR protocols, including 70k training and 2k testing samples, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The visual before/after check demonstrating how postprocessing fills SAM coverage gaps is removed. V2 instead provides DirectSAM segmentation examples across several images, without an ablation establishing the contribution of multiscale augmentation or a systematic robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The retained training curves do not introduce such reporting.

E6.justification: Qualitative segmentation results change from the SAM postprocessing example to DirectSAM outputs. The captioning curves and scores are unchanged: subobject/patch accuracies remain 88%/53% for size, 71%/50% for material, 80%/33% for shape and 63%/11% for counts. These retained results do not measure DirectSAM performance.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds an asymptotic argument that prompting-based segmentation requires O(N) decoder inference whereas DirectSAM requires O(1), with N defined as the number of subobjects. This is a new, brief complexity argument; no formal theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace SeqAE with DirectSAM as the highlighted architectural contribution, adding claims of faster, higher-quality and more comprehensive segmentation. SeqAE remains in the method, and the central claims about subobject tokenization improving captioning learning and accuracy are retained.

C2.justification: V2 introduces an efficiency-versus-comprehensiveness limitation for prompting-based SAM and explains DirectSAM through avoiding repeated decoding. It also explicitly states that DirectSAM-based LVLM results await future updates. Interpretations of the retained CLEVR results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Section 3.1 documents DirectSAM's 84.6M-parameter backbone, checkpoint, OpenCV contour processing, augmentation, resolutions, batch sizes, gradient accumulation, learning rates, hardware and approximately 15-plus-20-day training schedule. The abstract also changes code/model availability from a promised release to a stated release; existing SeqAE/LVLM details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for Suzuki–Abe contour detection, Pyramid of Captions and SegFormer, and positions DirectSAM against repeated prompting in SAM/MobileSAM. The broader subword-tokenization analogy and positioning relative to superpixels and vision-language models remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the segmentation subsection and parts of the abstract/introduction, adds a DirectSAM implementation subsection and adjusts headings and cross-references. Most SeqAE/LVLM prose and the overall introduction–method–experiment–conclusion structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The three-panel SAM postprocessing illustration is replaced by a large montage of DirectSAM boundary and segmentation outputs, and the SeqAE architecture diagram is removed entirely. The tokenization illustration, LVLM diagram and captioning-result display are retained, with the latter two renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a concrete segmentation method, substantial implementation information and qualitative outputs, while reporting code/model release. However, its newly prominent speed and quality claims lack timing or comparative segmentation measurements, and the unchanged CLEVR experiments still use MobileSAM-v2. Removing the SeqAE diagram also reduces architectural explanation. These benefits and weaknesses do not establish a reliable net improvement from the supplied PDFs.
